lesson.title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions in Real Life
lesson.description: Learn to add and subtract fractions with different denominators using real-life situations.
lesson.content:
A fraction shows part of a whole, like the amount of a chapati or a length of rope. To add or subtract fractions with different denominators, we first find a {{term:common denominator}} so the pieces are the same size.

Example: A farmer used $\frac{1}{2}$ of a bag of fertilizer on Monday and $\frac{1}{3}$ of a bag on Tuesday. Total used = $\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{3}{6}+\frac{2}{6}=\frac{5}{6}$ of a bag.

Example: A tailor had $\frac{3}{4}$ metre of cloth and used $\frac{1}{2}$ metre for a pocket. Cloth remaining = $\frac{3}{4}-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{3}{4}-\frac{2}{4}=\frac{1}{4}$ metre. Now try this: A pupil drank $\frac{2}{5}$ of a bottle of juice in the morning and $\frac{1}{5}$ in the afternoon. How much juice did the pupil drink in total?
